dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: sarvaṃ dehagataṃ dravyaṃ viyadvyāptaṃ mṛgekṣaṇe | vibhāvayet tatas tasya bhāvanā sā sthirā bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: O doe-eyed one, let one contemplate everything that makes up the body (bone, flesh and the rest) as pervaded by space; then that contemplation becomes steady.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: for one who cannot yet contemplate the void directly, this contemplation of the body's constituents (bone, flesh and so on) as pervaded by space steadies the contemplation of vacuity, which finally opens into the light of consciousness. Wallis: 'all the tissues of the body are pervaded by Space'.
dharana.technique_name: The Body's Tissues Pervaded by Space
dharana.instruction: Sense bone, flesh and every tissue of the body as filled through with space.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 47 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the body's tissues (bone, flesh and the rest)
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the whole body seen as porous: every tissue with space running all through it.
geometry.svg_hint: a body outline filled with fine dots and open gaps, like a sponge with light passing through
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Let space in
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: a body felt as dense and solid is felt as porous, and the mind steadies in that openness. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Let space soak through the whole body
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Space pervading bone, flesh and every tissue of the body

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: O doe-eyed one, let one contemplate everything that makes up the body (bone, flesh and the rest) as pervaded by space; then that contemplation becomes steady.
adiyogi.method_summary: Sense the body's tissues one after another (bone, muscle, blood, skin), each as pervaded by space, until the whole body feels porous and open. Rest there.

honesty.disclosure: Door 024 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 24 (verse 47) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 024 is dharana 24, verse 47. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If the image feels unpleasant, picture light or air passing through instead, or stop. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 024: the body's tissues pervaded by space. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 24, verse 47.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit or lie down. The map is the whole body, porous, with space running all through it.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes closed or soft.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Sense the bones as full of space, then the muscles, the blood, the skin. Let the whole body feel open. Rest there.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: a dense body becoming porous. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 47: contemplate all the substance of the body as pervaded by space, and the contemplation becomes steady.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Let the practice go. Take one free breath. Open the eyes and look around the room.
